neet_phy_u11_t06_1.working: Flux = E·A·cosθ = 200 × 0.5 × cos60° = 50 N m²/C. Option 4 has the wrong unit.

neet_phy_u11_t06_2.working: Imagine 8 cubes around the corner charge, so this cube gets q/8ε0. The 3 faces touching the corner carry zero flux (field lies in their plane). The 3 far faces share q/8ε0 equally, giving q/24ε0 each.

neet_phy_u11_t06_3.working: Charge enclosed = +3 − 5 = −2 μC; the outside charge does not count. Flux = −2×10⁻⁶ / 8.85×10⁻¹² ≈ −2.26×10⁵ N m²/C.

neet_phy_u11_t06_4.working: A is true: no charge is enclosed, so net flux is zero. R is a true fact, but A follows from Gauss's law or uniform-field geometry, not from flux being a scalar or its unit.

neet_phy_u11_t06_5.working: I is false: total flux stays q/ε0 by Gauss's law even though the field on the surface changes. II is true: a charge at a face centre sends half its flux into the cube, giving q/2ε0.
